help-area.title: Master Luthier’s help
help-area.text: Out of ducats and studies? The Master Luthier can help you: place 1 Lutherie token from your supply on the help area and receive 1 ducat or 1 study. Beware: this token stays locked there until the end of the game and will cost you 1 PP.
help.solo.title: Stradivarius board — level {level}
help.solo.text: You play against the Stradivarius bot as in a 2-player game. It has no hand and no sheet music: its turn plays itself. Its 3 Partner musicians are always sorted by decreasing Prestige.
help.solo.activity.text: The Note token on its track shows its activity level, from 1 to 4. Stradivarius only crafts on its Partner musicians of Prestige less than or equal to this level. It goes up by one at each Conservation.
help.solo.turn.text: It performs a Conservation if it meets the prerequisites of a musician of Prestige equal to its level + 1 (among its Partners or its Contacts), if one of its violins has no Lutherie token left, or if it has no room left to craft. Otherwise, it performs a Workshop.
help.solo.conservation.text: Its Crafting cards add a violin to its Heritage, with a Prestige equal to their number (4 at most). Its violins move to Heritage and its Lutherie tokens go to Ducats; yours come back to you. Then its activity level rises, it discards its musician with the lowest Prestige and takes one of the new level: from its Contacts if it meets the prerequisites, otherwise from the draw pile, placing 1 token on the help area (−1 PP).
help.solo.workshop.text: It crafts a quality 2 violin for free on its leftmost Partner musician of Prestige less than or equal to its level, on the lowest free slot, with no placement bonus. Then each Partner card gives it a bonus according to its affiliation: Wood, +1 quality to the placed violin; Study, +1 study; Relation, +1 card from the draw pile in its Contacts line.
help.solo.end-of-turn.text: Its violins wear like a player’s. Then each Restoration card restores a violin: first one of its own with no Lutherie token, otherwise one of yours, on the musician with the lowest Prestige, then the one with the highest quality, then the lowest slot. Its Lutherie tokens returned to it go to its Studies.
help.solo.piano.text: During Conservation, after moving to Heritage, it discards each pair of cards from its Contacts with the same affiliation (with no card of Prestige equal to its level + 1), starting from the left, and values by 1 its violin in Heritage with the highest Prestige below 4.
help.solo.forte.text: At the end of its Conservation, if it has 2 studies, it trains the leftmost apprentice of its Contacts line. Its apprentices add to its Workshop bonuses and score their PP at the end of the game (Relation: all the cards in its Contacts).
help.solo.fortissimo.text: You play first. Its Partners include a Prestige 2 musician and its Contacts an apprentice. Its Lutherie tokens go to Studies instead of Ducats. At the end of each Workshop, if it has a Prestige 4 musician holding a violin, it values by 1 its violin in Heritage with the highest Prestige below 4.
help.solo.contacts.text: Its Contacts form a line: every card is visible. When you draw, you may swap a card from your hand with any of its cards; your card takes its place.
help.solo.score.text: The Prestige of its violins (Partners and Heritage), the PP of its apprentices, plus half, rounded down, of its remaining ducats, studies and Contacts cards, minus 1 PP per token on the help area. You win if you have more PP; in case of a tie, the most violins crafted, then the most Partner apprentices. A perfect tie is a loss.

help.board.title: Board – {player}
help.sheet-music.text: The Note tokens form the programmed actions of the sheet music. They are placed on a beat and an action line. Consecutive notes on the same line form a single action, of as much time as there are notes. At the start of your turn, you may change your sheet music; each change costs 1 study.
help.note.title: Note token
help.note.move: Move a note to the line just above or just below. The Wood and Restoration lines are neighbours.
help.note.swap: Swap 2 consecutive notes without changing their action lines. The first and last notes count as consecutive.
help.note.shift: Shift all notes one beat to the right, the last note becoming the first of the sheet music; or to the left, the first note becoming the last of the sheet music.
help.ducats.text: Each Lutherie token placed in the Ducats area is worth 1 ducat.
help.wood-stock.text: The first token placed in the Wood stock area is a Violin token, representing a quality 1 wood. Each Lutherie token placed on the Violin token raises its quality by 1, up to quality 4, the maximum. At the end of the Workshop sequence, the wood in stock ages: add 1 Lutherie token on each stack, up to 4 tokens including the Violin token.
help.studies.text: Each Lutherie token placed in the Studies area is worth 1 study.
help.heritage.text: A Violin token placed in the Heritage area no longer wears; it scores as many PP as the Prestige of the musician it came from.
help.contacts.text: Your Contacts area is a personal reserve of cards from which you can draw the visible card of each pile. Your opponents may swap a card from their hand with a visible card of your Contacts. You cannot craft a violin for a musician in the Contacts area.
help.turn-discard.text: The cards discarded during your turn. At the end of the Workshop sequence, spread them as you like on top of the piles of your Contacts area.
help.partners.text: Partner musicians to the right of the board, Partner apprentices below. You can only play cards from your hand during a Conservation sequence or through a placement bonus when crafting a violin, meeting their conditions. You cannot train more than 6 apprentices during the game.
help.workshop.text: Resolve the actions of your sheet music from left to right. Then activate the end-of-turn effect of a single musician holding one of your Violin tokens, draw a card for each empty pile of your Contacts, spread the cards discarded this turn on top of your Contacts, then carry out the wear of all your violins and the aging of the wood in stock.
help.conservation.text: Move all your Violin tokens placed on musicians to your Heritage area, in the space matching the Prestige of the musician that held them: their Lutherie tokens are returned to their owners, who place them in their Ducats or Studies area. Then train or take back apprentices, and place or take back musicians.
help.master.title: Master Luthier board
help.master.text: It shows the Partner musicians of the Master Luthier who trained you. Each player may craft a violin for them by spending as many studies as their Prestige, in addition to the crafting time: 1 study for Prestige 1, 2 for Prestige 2, 3 for Prestige 3, 4 for Prestige 4.
help.help-area.text: At any time during the game, if a player needs a ducat or a study and has none, they may ask the Master Luthier for help. They place a Lutherie token from their supply on the help area and gain a ducat or a study. Each token on the help area is locked until the end of the game and will cost its owner 1 PP.
help.violin.title: Violin token – {player}
help.violin.text: This violin scores as many PP as the Prestige of its musician. It wears at the end of each of its owner’s Workshop sequences: the top Lutherie token of its stack is removed; if there is none left, the violin breaks and the Violin token returns to the supply. A restoration adds a Lutherie token to it, its quality never exceeding 4.
help.reserve.text: In its owner’s supply, ready for use.
help.lutherie.title: Lutherie token – {player}
help.lutherie.quality: Placed on a wood or a violin, it raises its quality by 1.
help.lutherie.returned: Returned to its owner: they will place it in their Ducats or Studies area.

help.starting.text: For a first game, each player chooses a Start card that shows them:
help.starting.notes: The placement of the 7 Note tokens on their sheet music: {notes}.
help.starting.musician: 1 Prestige 1 musician card to place in the Partner musicians area: {card}.
help.starting.contacts: 4 cards to place in the Contacts area: {cards}.
help.first-player.title: First player card
help.first-player.text: {player} starts the game. The end of the game is triggered when a player, at the end of their turn, has crafted their 12 violins: their opponents, up to the player seated to the right of the first player, play one last turn.
help.help-area.count: Help area: {count, plural, one {# locked token} other {# locked tokens}}
rules.starting-decks.title: First game: starting decks
rules.starting-decks.1: Each player chooses a Start card that shows them: the placement of the 7 Note tokens on their sheet music, 1 Prestige 1 musician card to place in the Partner musicians area, 3 cards to take into hand and 4 cards to place in the Contacts area.
rules.starting-decks.2: Finally, everyone starts with one Lutherie token in their Ducats area.
rules.mulligan.title: Mulligan
rules.mulligan.1: Each player receives 10 cards. Each player may, once, put any number of cards from their hand under the central draw pile and draw as many. From these 10 cards, each player chooses 7. The others are placed under the central draw pile.
rules.draft.title: Draft
rules.draft.1: Each player receives 8 cards. From these 8 cards, each player keeps 1 and passes the rest to their left neighbour. Repeat this process with the remaining cards. When each player has only 2 cards left, they keep one last card and the other is shuffled into the draw pile.
rules.starting-musician.title: Starting musician
rules.starting-musician.1: Starting with the first player, each player chooses the starting musician they want to begin with and places it in their Partners area.
rules.arrange.title: Contacts and sheet music
rules.arrange.1: Out of their 7 kept cards, each player places 4 to form their Contacts area and keeps the remaining 3 cards in hand.
rules.arrange.2: Building the sheet music: the affiliation of the selected cards (hand and Contacts) gives the 7 notes each player can place, one note per beat. The player chooses the order in which to place them.
rules.sheet-music.title: Start of the turn
rules.sheet-music.1: At the start of your turn, you may change your sheet music; each change costs 1 study. There can never be 2 notes on the same beat.
rules.sheet-music.2: Move a note to the line just above or just below. The Wood and Restoration lines are neighbours.
rules.sheet-music.3: Swap 2 consecutive notes without changing their action lines. The first and last notes count as consecutive.
rules.sheet-music.4: Shift all notes one beat to the right, the last note becoming the first of the sheet music; or to the left, the first note becoming the last of the sheet music.
rules.sheet-music.5: Then you have 2 options: perform a Workshop sequence, or a Conservation sequence.
rules.play-action.title: Sheet music action
rules.play-action.1: You carry out the actions ordered by your sheet music, from left to right, without being able to change their programming. You may skip an action or resolve it for less time. Consecutive notes on the same line give a single action whose strength equals its number of time.
rules.play-action.2: You may temporarily increase the time of the action being played by discarding cards from your hand affiliated with this type of action, each discarded card adding 1 time to this action. There is no limit to an action’s time.
rules.play-action.3: You may also benefit from the effect of your placed apprentices when resolving an action they are affiliated with. Each apprentice can be used only once per action, at any moment of its resolution.
rules.play-action.4: Wood action: pay 1 ducat to add 1 wood to your stock. The total number of tokens (Violin + Lutherie) equals the action’s time, 4 at most.
rules.play-action.5: Study action: take as many Lutherie tokens from your supply as the action’s time and place them in your Studies area.
rules.crafting.title: Crafting action
rules.crafting.1: Take a wood from your stock, whatever its quality. Then place it on a free slot of a musician of Prestige equal to or less than the action’s time. This wood is now a violin with a Prestige equal to the musician’s. It scores as many PP.
rules.crafting.2: 3 kinds of musicians can be used: a Partner musician; an opponent’s musician holding at least one of your tokens; a Master Luthier musician, for which you must spend as many studies as its Prestige in addition to the crafting time.
rules.crafting.3: Gain your violin’s placement bonus immediately: play a card from your hand meeting its prerequisites, draw a card, gain a study, raise the quality of the placed violin’s wood by 1, or gain a ducat.
rules.crafting.4: The Crafting action cannot be split: you cannot divide a Crafting action of several time into several weaker Crafting actions.
rules.relation.title: Relation action
rules.relation.1: There are 2 ways to resolve the action: either draw as many Character cards as the action’s time, or activate the Relation effect of a Musician card holding one of your violins, whether it is in your Partners area, on the Master Luthier board or in an opponent’s Partners area.
rules.relation.2: The Relation action used to activate an effect cannot be split: you cannot divide a Relation action of several time into several weaker Relation actions.
rules.draw.title: Drawing
rules.draw.1: Whenever a player must draw, they may choose to: take one of the 4 visible cards of their Contacts area; swap a card from their hand with a visible card among their opponents’ Contacts; draw the top card of the draw pile.
rules.draw.2: A player’s hand is limited to 10 cards at the end of their turn.
rules.restoration.title: Restoration action
rules.restoration.1: Add as many Lutherie tokens as the action’s time to the violins of your choice to improve the quality of their wood. You may restore the violins of any musician in play, including your opponents’.
rules.restoration.2: Spread the tokens as you like. The quality of a violin’s wood can never exceed 4.
rules.effect.title: Card effect
rules.effect.1: All effects and bonuses are optional. Gains may be taken in part. If an effect contradicts the rules, the effect wins.
rules.effect.2: Click a card to read its effect.
rules.reclaim.title: Running out of tokens
rules.reclaim.1: Lutherie tokens are limited: if a player runs out of them in their supply, they may take one from elsewhere on their board, from one of the 3 areas of their workshop (Ducats, Wood stock or Studies).
rules.returned.title: Returned tokens
rules.returned.1: Lutherie tokens are returned to their respective owners, who place them in their Ducats and/or Studies area as they choose.
rules.end-of-turn.title: End-of-turn effect
rules.end-of-turn.1: After resolving your sheet music, activate the end-of-turn effect of a single musician holding one of your Violin tokens.
rules.spread.title: Arrange your Contacts area
rules.spread.1: For each empty pile of your Contacts area, draw a card from the draw pile to fill it.
rules.spread.2: Spread the cards discarded this turn as you like on top of the piles of your Contacts area.
rules.aging.title: Wear and aging
rules.aging.1: Wear of all your violins: remove the top Lutherie token of the stack of each of your violins. If it is an opponent’s token, give it back to its owner, who makes it 1 ducat or 1 study; if it is one of yours, it returns to your supply. If there is no Lutherie token on your violin, it breaks: the Violin token returns to your supply.
rules.aging.2: Aging of the wood in stock: add 1 Lutherie token on your wood stacks in stock, up to 4 tokens including the Violin token.
rules.hand-limit.title: Hand limit
rules.hand-limit.1: A player’s hand is limited to 10 cards at the end of their turn.
rules.conservation.title: Conservation sequence
rules.conservation.1: Heritage: your Violin tokens placed on musicians go to your Heritage area, in the space matching the Prestige of the musician that held them. Their Lutherie tokens are returned to their owners, who place them in their Ducats and/or Studies area.
rules.conservation.2: Train or take back apprentices: place 1 or more apprentices from your hand if 3 consecutive actions of your sheet music exactly match the required pattern. You cannot train more than 6 apprentices during the game. You may also take placed apprentices back into your hand, giving up their end-of-game PP.
rules.conservation.3: Place or take back musicians: place 1 or more musicians from your hand if you meet their prerequisites. You may also take placed musicians back into your hand; the violins and Lutherie tokens on them are returned to their owners.
rules.turn.title: Game turn
rules.turn.1: Resolve the actions of your sheet music from left to right. Then activate the end-of-turn effect of a single musician holding one of your Violin tokens, draw a card for each empty pile of your Contacts, spread the cards discarded this turn on top of your Contacts, then carry out the wear of all your violins and the aging of the wood in stock.
rules.turn.2: Move all your Violin tokens placed on musicians to your Heritage area, in the space matching the Prestige of the musician that held them: their Lutherie tokens are returned to their owners, who place them in their Ducats or Studies area. Then train or take back apprentices, and place or take back musicians.
rules.final.title: End of the game
rules.final.1: The end of the game is triggered when a player, at the end of their turn, has crafted their 12 violins. Their opponents, up to the player seated to the right of the first player, play one last turn.
rules.final.2: Each player has a last chance to place apprentices to score their PP: they may first change their sheet music by spending the required studies, then place one or more apprentices if their sheet music allows it. Taking cards from the Partners area back into your hand is not allowed at this point of the game.
tuto.welcome: Welcome to <bold>Paneveggio</bold>! You are an apprentice luthier. Craft violins for musicians and earn Prestige points (PP). The game ends when a player has crafted their 12 violins.
tuto.theme: In 1700, the spruces of the Paneveggio forest, in Italy, provide the wood most sought after by luthiers such as Stradivari. You will craft, restore and preserve violins, and surround yourself with musicians and apprentices.
tuto.board:
This is your board. Above it, your Contacts; to the right, your Partner musicians and apprentices; below, your hand.
<italic>At any time, click an element to see what it is for.</italic>
tuto.sheet-music: Your sheet music has 7 beats, read from left to right. Each line is an action: Wood, Study, Crafting, Relation, Restoration. Consecutive notes on the same line form a single, stronger action: 2 notes = an action of 2 time.
tuto.change-sheet-music: At the start of your turn, you may change your sheet music: each change costs 1 study (move a note up or down, swap 2 consecutive notes, or shift all the notes). You have no study yet: keep it as it is.
tuto.tokens: Your 14 Lutherie tokens are your resources: in the Ducats area, each one is worth 1 ducat; in the Studies area, 1 study; and in your wood stock, they show the quality of the wood. You start with 1 ducat; the other tokens wait in your supply.
tuto.sequence:
Now choose your sequence. <bold>Workshop</bold>: play the actions of your sheet music. <bold>Conservation</bold>: put your violins in Heritage and play cards from your hand.
Choose <bold>Workshop</bold>.
tuto.wood:
Your first action is <bold>Wood</bold>, of 2 time: pay 1 ducat to add a wood to your stock. Its quality equals the action’s time (4 at most).
Do not resolve it yet: you will boost it first.
tuto.boost:
Before resolving an action, you may discard cards of the same type from your hand: each one adds 1 time to the action.
Discard card <bold>#4</bold> (Wood type): your Wood action goes up to 3 time.
tuto.resolve-wood: Click <bold>resolve it</bold>: you pay your ducat and receive a quality 3 wood.
tuto.wood-stock: Your wood is in your stock: 1 Violin token and 2 Lutherie tokens, so quality 3.
tuto.study:
<bold>Study</bold> action: place as many Lutherie tokens in your Studies area as the action’s time. Studies pay for sheet music changes and for the Master Luthier’s musicians.
Click <bold>resolve it</bold>.
tuto.crafting:
<bold>Crafting</bold> action: place a wood from your stock on a free slot of a musician whose Prestige is at most the action’s time.
Click <bold>resolve it</bold>.
tuto.crafting-slot: Your Noble has Prestige 1: place your wood on its bottom slot. Each slot gives a bonus: this one, 1 ducat.
tuto.violin: Your wood has become a violin. It is worth its musician’s Prestige: 1 PP.
tuto.master-luthier: You can also craft for an opponent’s musician holding one of your tokens, or for the Master Luthier’s musicians: they cost as many studies as their Prestige.
tuto.wood-again:
New <bold>Wood</bold> action, of 1 time: with the ducat you just gained, buy a quality 1 wood.
Click <bold>resolve it</bold>.
tuto.relation:
<bold>Relation</bold> action: draw as many cards as the action’s time, or use the Relation effect of a musician holding one of your violins.
Click <bold>resolve it</bold>.
tuto.contacts:
You draw from the draw pile, from your Contacts, or by swapping a card from your hand with an opponent’s Contact.
Take <bold>Tessarini</bold> from your Contacts.
tuto.restoration:
<bold>Restoration</bold> action: add Lutherie tokens to any violins, even your opponents’ (quality 4 at most). Restored violins last longer.
Click <bold>resolve it</bold>.
tuto.restore: Click your violin to add a token to it: its quality goes up to 4.
tuto.spread:
Your Workshop is over. The cards discarded this turn are spread over your Contacts piles: you can draw them later.
Place card #4 on the empty pile.
tuto.wear: Then each of your violins wears: its top token is removed. A violin with no Lutherie token breaks. Finally, the wood in your stock ages: +1 quality.
tuto.help-area: Missing a ducat or a study? Click the Master Luthier’s help area: one of your tokens is locked there until the end of the game (−1 PP), and you receive 1 ducat or 1 study.
tuto.opponent: Lionel’s turn. He chooses a Conservation and trains an apprentice.
tuto.heritage: Your violin goes to Heritage: it no longer wears and always counts for its Prestige. Its Lutherie tokens come back to you.
tuto.returned-tokens: Each token that comes back to you becomes, as you choose, a ducat or a study. Take a ducat, then a study.
tuto.apprentice:
You can now train apprentices: 3 consecutive actions of your sheet music must follow their pattern (6 apprentices at most). Apprentice <bold>#15</bold> requires Crafting, Wood, Relation: that is the case.
Place it.
tuto.musicians:
You could also place musicians whose violin requirements you meet, or take Partners back into your hand.
Finish your Conservation.
tuto.end-of-game: When a player has crafted their 12 violins, the round is completed, then everyone has a last chance to change their sheet music and train apprentices. Scoring: your violins (in Heritage and on musicians), plus your apprentices’ points, minus 1 PP per token on the help area.
tuto.good-luck:
You know the essentials. Continue the game against Lionel. Have fun!
<italic>At any time, click an element or the “?” in the banner to find the rules again.</italic>
